scope: Actual H200 Muse NVFP4 expert path; expert all-reduce, scheduler, attention, draft model excluded from local measurements

assessment.finding: Generic, tightly optimized legacy tensor-core machinery with plausible specialization opportunities; code size alone is not proof of runtime waste.
not_runtime_waste_by_itself: Zero-point, activation-order, bias and scale-format branches use compile-time conditions/specializations; deleting their source need not change generated instructions.
torch.empty allocations before graph capture do not imply repeated device allocation during graph replay.
Virtual scratch capacity does not equal bytes touched; nonlocal slots are masked and may remain unwritten.
assessment.real_measured_bottleneck: Both Marlin GEMMs contribute 92.3-95.1% of profiled expert replay at M128/256/384/512.

implementation.mechanism: NVFP4 weights are repacked for Marlin; E4M3 scales are permuted; expert global scales are converted to activation dtype. This is outside timed replay.
Map global expert IDs to local IDs, using -1 for nonlocal slots. Sort/pad slots by expert to an M tile. Selected guarded policy caps M tiles at16 through M256,32 through M512.
cache1 stores gate/up output at [M*8,8192]; cache2 stores activated [M*8,4096]; cache3 aliases cache1 storage for down output. FP32 cross-CTA scratch and lock workspace are separate.
implementation.capacity: cache13 + cache2 = 196608*M bytes at the fixed model dimensions; 48 MiB at M256, excluding FP32 scratch. This is capacity, not measured traffic.

implementation.mechanism: Sparse expert routing gathers BF16 input rows while reading repacked FP4 expert weights. Output width8192 combines gate and up.

Two candidate thread configurations for M<=16 and two for larger M. Select the valid configuration with greatest estimated resident block count; this heuristic does not directly optimize measured latency.

Fixed SM-count-scaled grid traverses roughly equal stripes over (expert-M-block,N-tile,K-tile). Stripes can split an output tile along K. Each CTA counts valid EP blocks, then locates blocks and reloads route metadata.

Four-stage cp.async pipeline moves gathered activations, packed weights and scale metadata through shared memory. FP4 E2M1 and FP8 E4M3 scales are decoded to BF16 fragments, multiplied, then fed to warp-level mma.sync m16n8k16 with FP32 accumulators. This path does not use Hopper WGMMA.

Only split slices need cross-CTA reduction. The selected path keeps FP32 partials in scratch and serializes ordered reduction through locks. Final output converts to BF16, then applies BF16 expert global scale.
Separate masked SwiGLU writes cache2; second Marlin call computes width4096 using the same aligned expert slots, with top_k=1 over expanded rows.

One Triton program per token loops over its eight slots, skips nonlocal slots, applies the effective norm weight before per-expert RMSNorm, accumulates routing-weighted outputs in FP32, and stores BF16.

hotspots_and_constraints.issue: Repeated valid-expert scan and route metadata barriers in every CTA and both GEMMs
hotspots_and_constraints.counter_or_probe: Source instruction/stall attribution plus isolated compact metadata variant; earlier alignment/skip ablations were not useful, so do not assume a large gain.

hotspots_and_constraints.issue: Padding and gathered activation accesses reduce useful tensor-core work
hotspots_and_constraints.classification: measured M-tile sensitivity; remaining inefficiency unquantified
hotspots_and_constraints.counter_or_probe: Compare valid rows to padded rows, DRAM/L2 bytes, tensor pipe activity across routing skew and M; preserve same input distribution.

hotspots_and_constraints.issue: FP4/scale decode instructions compete with math and loading
hotspots_and_constraints.counter_or_probe: Instruction mix, issue utilization, dependency stalls, tensor throughput. Compare SASS before/after; retain weight scaling/rounding behavior.

hotspots_and_constraints.issue: Stripe split-K partial traffic and lock dependency chains
hotspots_and_constraints.classification: conditional work only when slice_count>1; not every output uses global reduction
hotspots_and_constraints.counter_or_probe: Quantify split-slice fraction and scratch bytes before replacing schedule. A complete-K CTA can remove locks but may underfill the GPU on small workloads.

hotspots_and_constraints.issue: Fixed four-stage pipeline and occupancy-driven dispatch
hotspots_and_constraints.classification: hardware profiles support coupled register/shared-memory constraint; causal speedup remains unproven
hotspots_and_constraints.counter_or_probe: M8 shared-memory limit3 vs register limit4; M128 both limits3. Evaluate stage/lifetime coupling, not a stage-count-only occupancy assumption.

hotspots_and_constraints.classification: remaining fraction small at larger decode shapes
hotspots_and_constraints.counter_or_probe: Measure actual intermediate traffic and finalizer kernel time. Dense allocation capacity is not an 8x optimization opportunity.

estimation_contract.reference: Current selected expert method, not original stock and not full serving
estimation_contract.range_semantics: Conditional successful-candidate envelope; every unmeasured change can yield zero gain, regress, or fail correctness. These are prioritization guesses, not expected values.
estimation_contract.confidence_semantics: Qualitative confidence that an experiment can find useful expert-path improvement; not calibrated probability.
estimation_contract.cost_semantics: Rough focused engineering hours plus H200 experiment hours; excludes billed idle time. Agent throughput may differ.
estimation_contract.composition: Do not add or multiply estimated gains blindly; candidates overlap and may remove the same cost.
estimation_contract.serving_conversion: S_serving = 1/((1-f_expert)+f_expert/S_expert); f_expert is currently unknown. No numeric serving-speedup estimate is defensible yet.

roi_queue.name: Nsight counter baseline + generated-code audit
roi_queue.status: baseline M8/M128 captured; extend only to resolve specific uncertainty
roi_queue.why: Avoid further blind tile enumeration. Determine whether memory, decode/issue, synchronization, or tensor compute dominates at M8 and128; add M256/large prefill if the regime differs.
roi_queue.deliverable: Captured counter JSON available; next diagnosis should inspect dependency/issue/SASS evidence and rerun affected shape after a candidate.

roi_queue.name: Coupled NVFP4 pipeline-depth and register-lifetime specialization
roi_queue.status: ready for isolated design using counters
roi_queue.confidence: medium bottleneck hypothesis; low-medium gain prior
roi_queue.why: M128 uses155 registers/thread and77.482KB shared/block; both resources limit residency to3 CTAs/SM. M8 uses128 registers/thread, register limit4 but shared limit3. Sweep stage count only with consistent SMEM accounting and register lifetime changes; verify latency hiding is not lost. Dequantization/dependency scheduling may matter more than residency alone.
roi_queue.kill_condition: No reduction in attributable instruction/stall cost or no holdout gain; deleting already-compiled-away generic code does not qualify.
counter_gates: Measure registers, shared memory, spills, eligible warps, tensor activity and clean paired time.
At M128, reducing stages alone may leave the register limit at3 CTAs; no claim of higher residency without measured launch attributes.
Do not trade FP32 accumulator/reduction precision for register reduction.

roi_queue.name: Complete-K grouped work queue with compact expert metadata
roi_queue.why: Compute work descriptors once, dispatch valid expert output tiles directly, and avoid inter-CTA reductions when output-tile parallelism suffices. Keep a split-K fallback for genuinely small workloads.
risks: Too little parallelism at low M
roi_queue.kill_condition: Too few split slices or metadata cycles to justify queue construction; earlier skip-nonlocal ablation alone did not establish a gain.

roi_queue.name: Hopper-specific grouped WGMMA pipeline
roi_queue.status: requires R01 tensor/issue evidence and bounded prototype
roi_queue.why: Separate producer/dequantization and tensor-core consumers; stage dequantized BF16 weights in shared memory and use warp-group MMA for sufficiently large expert groups. Prefer a bounded prefill/large-M prototype before replacing sparse decode.
risks: Additional shared-memory traffic can erase gain
Small expert groups underfill warp-group tiles
FP32 reduction/global-scale BF16 rounding must remain equivalent enough to pass the unchanged oracle
No assumption of native Hopper NVFP4 tensor math
roi_queue.kill_condition: Prototype cannot outperform current grouped path after conversion, scheduling, and scratch overhead are included.

roi_queue.name: Gate/up epilogue plus SwiGLU fusion
roi_queue.status: requires measured intermediate traffic and R03 scheduling feasibility
roi_queue.why: Can remove a launch and intermediate read/write if gate/up output halves are co-owned and fully reduced. Existing N tiles usually own only one slice, so this is not a trivial epilogue toggle.
risks: Gate and up are separate output halves
Cross-CTA K partials must finish before nonlinear activation
Preserve BF16 intermediate rounding and global-scale order
roi_queue.kill_condition: Pairing outputs increases registers/SMEM or duplicates work more than saved materialization.

roi_queue.name: Finalizer launch geometry / cooperative norm reduction
roi_queue.status: defer large-M; consider low-M if measured share warrants
roi_queue.why: Current one-program-per-token scheme may underfill at M1/8, but fusion already captured the obvious launch win. Full hidden-width RMSNorm blocks direct fusion into independent down-GEMM output tiles.
roi_queue.kill_condition: No stable total-expert improvement; finalizer-only gains are not enough.

roi_queue.name: Workspace reuse / graph bucket memory reduction
roi_queue.status: defer until allocation/zeroing appears in measured critical path
roi_queue.why: May help memory footprint or uncaptured execution, but graph replay avoids Python allocator work. Do not prioritize on allocation count alone.

roi_queue.name: Full serving trace and cross-component optimization
roi_queue.why: Measure expert critical-path fraction, collectives/rank skew, attention context regimes, DFlash acceptance and graph coverage, and scheduler/prefix-cache effects. A 3x overall target cannot be established from expert proxies.

parked_evidence.idea: independent gate/up and down M tiles
parked_evidence.reason: Four tested pairs all regressed meaningful decode shapes.

parked_evidence.idea: force existing wider N/K configs or lower persistent block count globally
parked_evidence.reason: ~4% at M512 accompanied by regressions at primary M8/32/128/256; guarded M512 tweak is low priority for the 3x objective.
No decode gain; meaningful regressions M32/128/256. Do not enumerate nearby tiles without new counter evidence.

rewrite_stages.output: Counter attribution, SASS/register/SMEM inventory, active/padded route distribution
rewrite_stages.gate: Repeatable incumbent control; no speedup claims from profiler timings.

rewrite_stages.output: One bottleneck-specific isolated patch or standalone faithful prototype
rewrite_stages.gate: Same prepared model weights/layout or explicitly accounted lossless repack; no omitted routing/norm/precision work.

rewrite_stages.output: Screen by every primary shape plus boundaries and representative prefill
rewrite_stages.gate: Fixed incumbent, paired alternating runs, enough samples to establish noninferiority; profile separately.

rewrite_stages.output: Frozen candidate + independent seeds/sessions + adverse routing
rewrite_stages.gate: Numerical oracle, no-local eager and captured replay, stale-buffer tests, all-shape regression policy; retain failed attempts.

rewrite_stages.output: Integrated serving patch with reproducible source and build hashes
rewrite_stages.gate: Patch restrictions and independent review; full model agreement, TTFT and official interactivity/throughput curve remain mandatory.

precision_and_fusion_invariants: Retain BF16 activation boundaries and FP32 MMA/reduction behavior; replacing reduction scratch with BF16 atomics is not an accepted shortcut.
Preserve E2M1/E4M3 scaling semantics, expert global-scale representation and final-output conversion order. Reassociation may change rounding; test against the same reference and model-output gate.
Apply each expert norm before routing-weighted summation. Norm(weighted_sum(expert_outputs)) is not equivalent.
Do not apply routing weights twice or before a nonlinear stage without proof.
Nonlocal/unwritten expert slots must remain masked; fully nonlocal rows must return exact zeros even after valid captured replays.
The model-specific Marlin fallback relies on post-expert normalization and scale preparation; preserve that contract, including epsilon behavior.
No host input-value synchronization in captured execution. Device-side routing/work queues must remain graph safe.
A rewrite must include its gather, layout conversion, scratch initialization and epilogue costs in timed execution unless identical work is legitimately moved to model preparation.

threefold_feasibility.interpretation: Requires roughly 3.34-3.60x faster GEMMs at these measured profiles if other work stays fixed; incremental metadata/finalizer cleanup cannot establish 3x expert speedup.
threefold_feasibility.full_serving: Unknown expert fraction and overlapping work. Preserve the 3x target but do not claim it is feasible or achieved from these priors.

rsi_handoff.planner: Choose the next candidate from attributable cost and expected information/engineering cost; report which prior changed after each measurement.
rsi_handoff.implementer: One isolated bottleneck hypothesis, owned code paths, frozen baseline and explicit cost accounting.
rsi_handoff.measurement_owner: Exclusive GPU execution; immutable evidence bundle; profiles separated from clean timing.
rsi_handoff.critic: Reject invalid model/precision changes, omitted costs, narrowed success criteria, and reused tuning seeds as holdout.
rsi_handoff.promotion_owner: Independent source review and all predeclared gates; do not modify protected goals/oracle/holdout suite to make a candidate pass.

hardware_evidence.scope: Nsight hardware-counter captures, cold kernel replay; profiler durations not clean timing. Single routing sample/seed per batch.
hardware_evidence.inference: Neither captured case simply saturates DRAM or tensor compute. Resource/dependency scheduling is a plausible target, not proven causal attribution. Low occupancy alone does not prove an optimization; compare unchanged control, counters and clean time.
